value: You create a /27 subnet called AzureBastionSubnet for a new Standard Bastion. Is it large enough?
reason: "Will the deployment's subnet meet the requirement?" reads awkwardly; ask the plain question.

value: Since 2 November 2021 the minimum is /26; only Bastions already deployed on /27 before that date keep working unchanged.
reason: "that date" pointed at nothing on the card; the source gives November 2, 2021.

value: Production needs a dedicated Bastion deployment, and security policy forbids it any public IP address. Which SKU must you deploy?
reason: Bastion Developer also has no public IP ("except Bastion Developer and Private-only"), so the old front had two defensible answers.

value: Inbound traffic through a subnet and network interface with no NSG is blocked, so an NSG rule must allow it.
reason: The same source says outbound traffic from VM4 "flows freely" with no NSG; the unqualified claim read as both directions.

value: The Azure DNS resource, named after your domain (such as contoso.com), in which you create and manage the domain's DNS records.
reason: "holds the DNS records ... once the domain is delegated" implied records exist only after delegation; the tutorial creates records before delegating.

value: Once the domain is delegated to the zone at the registrar, internet users resolving names in the domain are directed to it.
reason: Moves delegation to the explanation, where the tutorial puts it.

value: A group of DNS records in a zone; Azure DNS sets the TTL for the whole group, not for each record.
reason: The cited TTL text supports only the TTL; "named collection" and "settings such as the TTL" rest on the uncached include file.

value: So every record within a record set uses the same TTL value.
reason: "Azure DNS manages records in sets" goes beyond the TTL passage; keep to what it says.

value: Records that need different TTLs can't share one record set, because the TTL is set for the set.
reason: "You would need the records in different record sets" suggests two A record sets with the same name, which a newcomer would read as allowed.

value: A VM pings an internal Standard Load Balancer's frontend and gets no reply, though TCP traffic through it works. It has no HA ports rule. What explains it?
reason: A public Standard Load Balancer frontend does answer ping while a backend is healthy (load-balancer-test-frontend-reachability.md); the ICMP limit applies to internal load balancers without HA ports.

value: Its load-balancing and inbound NAT rules carry TCP or UDP only; an internal load balancer handles ICMP only with HA ports.
reason: Matches the corrected front and the components limitation text.

value: Load Balancer balances specific TCP or UDP protocols, not other IP protocols such as ICMP.
reason: Keeps the explanation to the cited limitation.

value: The frontend is the address clients use, so whether it is public or private decides who can reach the load balancer.
reason: "the only thing that separates the two" is an overstatement the source doesn't make.

value: Each frontend is its own IP address and point of contact for clients.
reason: "Each can serve its own rules" isn't in the cited section.

value: No: only the activity log stores a resource's creator, and it keeps events for just 90 days unless exported.
reason: "Probably not" hedges where the source is definite ("the only place that stores the creator", 90 days).

value: Each plotted point is the mean of all values captured in that time grain, such as all server response times.
reason: "The source's server response time example uses it" explains nothing; the source says each data point is the average of all captured response times.

value: A disaster recovery drill that creates the VM in the target region from a chosen recovery point, to check failover works.
reason: "without affecting replication" is not in the drill tutorial; it says the drill checks "that failover works as expected".

value: During those 14 days the deleted backup item can be recovered with no data loss.
reason: "enabled by default on new vaults" is not in the cited vault overview (it is in the create-vault article).
